candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — immunization and preventive health teaching
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — travel immunization
candidate.educational_objective: Use individualized pretravel assessment to determine routine, recommended, and required vaccines for international travel.

options.A: Use the same travel-vaccine list for every traveler because destination and itinerary do not affect recommendations.
options.B: Assume routine childhood immunizations cover all destination-specific vaccine-preventable risks encountered abroad.
options.C: Wait until after arrival at the destination because pretravel vaccination and consultation provide little preventive benefit.
options.D: Review destination, itinerary, timing, activities, health history, and routine-vaccine status during a pretravel consultation, then arrange recommended or required vaccines as indicated.

candidate.rationale: CDC Yellow Book guidance emphasizes individualized pretravel risk assessment based on destination, itinerary, timing, activities, and traveler health, followed by review of routine, recommended, and required vaccines. A through C ignore destination-specific risk assessment or the preventive purpose of pretravel care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Pretravel vaccine recommendations depend on individualized destination/itinerary/timing/health assessment and include routine, recommended, and required vaccines.
candidate.source_document_title: CDC Yellow Book 2026 — The Pre-Travel Consultation
candidate.source_locator: Components of a Pre-Travel Consultation — Assess individual risk; Manage risk — Vaccinations; Box 1.1.1
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
